answers.answer:
Histones H2A, H2B, H3 and H4 sit in SCOPe 2.08 class a (all-alpha), fold a.22 Histone-fold, superfamily a.22.1 Histone-fold, family a.22.1.1 Nucleosome core histones. The other proteins SCOPe places in the same fold and superfamily are: (1) family a.22.1.2 Archaeal histone (for example Methanothermus fervidus histone A and B under sunid 68897, plus Pyrococcus horikoshii and Methanopyrus kandleri species nodes); (2) family a.22.1.3 TBP-associated factors (TAFs), including TAF(II)135/hTAF4, TAF(II)20/hTAF12, TAF(II)42, TAF(II)62, TAF(II)18 and TAF(II)28, together with the histone-fold domain of Son of sevenless (sunid 101107), which SCOPe files here; (3) family a.22.1.4 Bacterial histone-fold protein (sunid 101318, e.g. Aquifex aeolicus Aq_328). Some a.22.1.1 nodes are only 'automated matches' (sunid 193445) and are not curated family assignments.

How strong each level is: the fold (a.22) groups proteins by shared histone-fold topology, a three-helix core that pairs in handshake dimers; this is structural similarity without a claim of common descent. The superfamily (a.22.1) is the level where SCOPe asserts probable common evolutionary origin, so histones, archaeal histones, TAFs and bacterial histone-fold proteins are distant homologs. The families (a.22.1.1 to a.22.1.4) are where closer homology is asserted, so relationships between families hold only at superfamily strength. Do not transfer function across families. TAFs are TFIID subunits that bind TBP and promoter DNA rather than packaging DNA into nucleosomes, and the function of the Sos histone domain and of the bacterial histone-fold proteins is not established by this classification.

Linker histones H1/H5 (family a.4.5.13, e.g. yeast Hho1p, sunid 101037) are functional analogs of core histones in chromatin compaction. They are in class a but in a different fold, a.4.5 (winged helix), so SCOPe does not treat them as histone-fold relatives. Any link to histones is functional, not evolutionary, in this classification.

Lexical hits are not relatives. HDAC7 and HDAC8 (c.42.1.2) and the Dot1l catalytic domain (c.66.1.31) match the word 'histone' because they act on histones, but they are class c alpha/beta folds with no histone-fold relationship.

Limits: this uses SCOPe 2.08 (freeze 2021). A periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16 exists, and I did not check what changed in it. The 'histone' search is paginated (has_more true, truncated) and I read only the first page, so the list is not exhaustive. A classification gives no sequence identity, DNA-binding or functional result; those need structure comparison, sequence-based homology search, or experimental evidence.

The other proteins SCOPe places in the same fold and superfamily are: (1) family a.22.1.2 Archaeal histone (for example Methanothermus fervidus histone A and B under sunid 68897, plus Pyrococcus horikoshii and Methanopyrus kandleri species nodes); (2) family a.22.1.3 TBP-associated factors (TAFs), including TAF(II)135/hTAF4, TAF(II)20/hTAF12, TAF(II)42, TAF(II)62, TAF(II)18 and TAF(II)28, together with the histone-fold domain of Son of sevenless (sunid 101107), which SCOPe files here; (3) family a.22.1.4 Bacterial histone-fold protein (sunid 101318, e.g. Aquifex aeolicus Aq_328). Some a.22.1.1 nodes are only 'automated matches' (sunid 193445) and are not curated family assignments.

How strong each level is: the fold (a.22) groups proteins by shared histone-fold topology, a three-helix core that pairs in handshake dimers; this is structural similarity without a claim of common descent. The superfamily (a.22.1) is the level where SCOPe asserts probable common evolutionary origin, so histones, archaeal histones, TAFs and bacterial histone-fold proteins are distant homologs. The families (a.22.1.1 to a.22.1.4) are where closer homology is asserted, so relationships between families hold only at superfamily strength. Do not transfer function across families. TAFs are TFIID subunits that bind TBP and promoter DNA rather than packaging DNA into nucleosomes, and the function of the Sos histone domain and of the bacterial histone-fold proteins is not established by this classification.

Linker histones H1/H5 (family a.4.5.13, e.g. yeast Hho1p, sunid 101037) are functional analogs of core histones in chromatin compaction. They are in class a but in a different fold, a.4.5 (winged helix), so SCOPe does not treat them as histone-fold relatives. Any link to histones is functional, not evolutionary, in this classification.

Lexical hits are not relatives. HDAC7 and HDAC8 (c.42.1.2) and the Dot1l catalytic domain (c.66.1.31) match the word 'histone' because they act on histones, but they are class c alpha/beta folds with no histone-fold relationship.

Limits: this uses SCOPe 2.08 (freeze 2021). A periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16 exists, and I did not check what changed in it. The 'histone' search is paginated (has_more true, truncated) and I read only the first page, so the list is not exhaustive. A classification gives no sequence identity, DNA-binding or functional result; those need structure comparison, sequence-based homology search, or experimental evidence.
